key_insight: An analytical model links capacitance–frequency measurements to ionic relaxation and predicts the scan-rate window of maximum current–voltage hysteresis in perovskite solar cells.
engineering_relevance: Routine impedance measurements could provide a computationally efficient route to quantify ion transport and assess device hysteresis.
method: Model the transition from low-frequency ion-screened depletion capacitance to high-frequency geometric capacitance, accounting for interlayer effects.
Use the characteristic transition frequency to determine the ionic dielectric relaxation time.
Relate capacitance–frequency behavior to scan-rate-dependent current–voltage hysteresis.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports excellent agreement with drift–diffusion simulations across varied ionic and transport-layer parameters, plus experimental confirmation of the capacitance–hysteresis correlation.
watch_item: Parameter extraction depends on correctly identifying the modeled capacitance transition; the abstract does not specify robustness when other device responses overlap.
paper_title: Analytical Framework Relating Capacitance-Frequency Measurements and Hysteresis in Perovskite Solar Cells
